sections.h2: Who handles a property tax bill in Will County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Will County is one of the five collar counties around Chicago, spread over 849 square miles with Joliet as its seat and biggest city. Cook and Iroquois counties gave up territory to create it on January 12, 1836. By the 2020 census it held 696,355 people, fourth highest among Illinois counties. The Du Page, Des Plaines and Kankakee rivers run through it, and the Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie, about 17,000 acres on the former Joliet Arsenal, sits inside its lines.

Four offices shape a bill. The Treasurer and the Board of Review both operate from the Will County Office Building, 302 N. Chicago Street, Joliet.

  • The Treasurer receives payments, conducts the yearly tax sale and sends the bills.
  • The Supervisor of Assessments coordinates with the township assessors who set values.
  • The Board of Review, second floor, rules on complaints about assessments.
  • The County Clerk accepts redemption money once a sale has happened.

The cities are Joliet, Aurora, Naperville, Lockport, Crest Hill, Braidwood and Wilmington. Villages run from Bolingbrook, Plainfield and Romeoville to Frankfort, Mokena, New Lenox and Peotone. Several straddle county lines, so find out which county actually bills the parcel.

sections.h2: Where do Will County home costs sit against the national picture?
sections.html:
Across 2020 to 2024 the typical Will County home was valued at $319,600, a bit below the U.S. figure of $332,700. Owners live in 82.8% of homes, and household income at the midpoint is $109,984.

The average commute takes 31.4 minutes, compared with 26.4 across the country. Four Metra lines link the county to the Chicago Loop, Amtrak stops at Joliet, and interstates 55, 57, 80 and 355 all pass through. Joliet Junior College, which serves the county, is described as the first two-year college in the nation.

sections.h2: When does a Will County installment turn delinquent?
sections.html:
Section 21-15 of the Property Tax Code treats the first installment as late once the later of June 1 or the day after the printed date has passed, and applies September 1 the same way to the second. Because Will has under 3,000,000 residents, the interest is 1.5% per month or part of a month.

The same section keeps a mailed check on time if it carries a postmark by the due date. It also shifts interest to a mortgage lender that held enough escrow and still let the bill lapse. Confirm with your servicer that a bill was actually paid.

The Treasurer runs a free e-notice program for paperless bills. Enroll at enoticesonline.com using the authorization code printed on your newest bill, after which the paper copy stops. Owners who lost the code can get a new one from the Treasurer's office.

sections.h2: Where and how can Will County taxes be paid?
sections.html:
Beyond the online portal, the Treasurer lists these routes, and paying by check carries no charge.

  • Mail a check to 302 N. Chicago St., Joliet, IL 60432, made out to the Will County Treasurer, with a return envelope if you want a receipt.
  • Walk into any of the 100-plus bank branches enrolled in the county program.
  • Call 815-680-2953. Drawing from a checking or savings account is free, and other payment types add convenience fees.
  • Visit the Treasurer's office, which takes cash, checks and cards. Subsequent taxes are accepted there only, weekdays from 8:30 until 3:30, with no exceptions.
  • Use the secure drop box at the Will County Building when the office is closed.

sections.h2: How does a Will County assessment complaint move forward?
sections.html:
For 2026 the Board of Review accepted complaints from August 12 through September 14, and its process opens every August. State law frames the deadline as 30 calendar days after publication of the list. The Board suggests asking your township assessor about any change in value before you file.

Every parcel needs its own complaint unless the parcels are contiguous and share a land use. The form must carry the parcel number, the address, a signature, the owner's mailing address and a daytime phone number. The Board's office, at 302 N. Chicago Street on the second floor, answers at (815) 740-4707.

Hearings come with house rules. Check the Board's portal 48 hours ahead to see whether yours is live, allow 15 minutes for the building's security screening, and know that a late arrival cannot be rescheduled. The Board decides on evidence using the cost, market and income approaches, so bring sales of comparable homes or an appraisal.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply in Will County?
sections.html:
Cook County touches Will County, which lifts the dollar caps above the statewide minimums.

  • General homestead: up to $8,000 off equalized assessed value for a county next to one of 3,000,000 or more (section 15-175).
  • Senior citizens: up to $8,000 once an owner is 65, under the same adjacency rule (section 15-170).
  • Low-income senior freeze (section 15-172), which has its own income test.

The county's property tax pages carry a section for exemptions and deferrals, and the Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral Act offers older owners a separate route. After a sale, the exemption holds through that assessment year, and the new owner may have to apply.

sections.h2: What is the Will County tax sale, and can taxes be redeemed?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's page explains that delinquent taxes put a lien on the property and are sold to investors, called tax buyers, at an annual sale. Bidders name the interest rate they will accept, and the lowest rate wins. What changes hands is a claim on the tax debt, and the home stays with the owner.

That page says owners typically get one to three years after the sale to redeem before a buyer may begin court action, while section 21-350 sets three years with exceptions. The County Clerk's tax redemption department collects redemption payments, usually beginning one to two weeks after the sale.

The Treasurer's annual tax sales page links information for property owners and instructions for subsequent taxes. Read it before listing a house that has fallen behind.

sections.h2: What should a Will County seller do about taxes at closing?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the Treasurer and have the title company confirm each open tax year. If a year was sold, redemption runs through the County Clerk, so the title agent should look for that too.

  • Take the parcel number from the bill and note the township.
  • See whether a homestead or senior exemption is on the bill and let the buyer know.
  • Clear open installments, plus the 1.5% monthly interest, from the proceeds.
  • Record the deed with the Recorder of Deeds, whose fees and transfer tax rules appear on the county recorder page.

Inherited houses and rentals add title work, and back tax can delay the closing, so bring it up with the closing agent from day one.

faqs.q: When does a Will County bill become late?
faqs.a: Delinquency begins after the later of June 1 or the printed date for the first installment, and after the later of September 1 or its printed date for the second. Interest then runs at 1.5% a month.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Will County tax face to face?
faqs.a: At the Treasurer's office inside the Will County Building, 302 N. Chicago Street, Joliet, which takes cash, checks and cards. A drop box at the building covers after-hours checks.

faqs.q: Can I contest my Will County assessment?
faqs.a: Yes, through a complaint to the Board of Review filed parcel by parcel. The 2026 window ran from August 12 through September 14, and the Board's number is (815) 740-4707.

faqs.q: What is the Will County homestead cap?
faqs.a: Up to $8,000 off equalized assessed value, since Will borders Cook County. Owners 65 and older can take a separate senior exemption, also capped at $8,000.

faqs.q: What if my Will County taxes were sold?
faqs.a: You can still redeem by paying the County Clerk's tax redemption department before the period ends. The Treasurer describes it as typically one to three years, and the statute allows three years from the sale, with exceptions.
